brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.

requirements.evidence: The bases are stacked on levels 0, 1 and 2: piece:0,0,0/1/2 (full) and piece:0,1,0/1/2 (half-n), joined by snaps.
There are three classic drawers, one per storey: drawer:0#0,1#cut, drawer:1#0,1#cut and drawer:2#0,1#cut, all facing the user's side.
capOpenFaces added 14 solid caps and lockJoints added a joint bolt. check_build is ok and the mesh check reads clear.

finish.summary:
I built a three-storey cabinet. The back column is three full hex bases stacked at q0 r0, levels 0 to 2. In front of it, at q0 r1, are three north-half bases stacked the same way. Each half base has a classic drawer on its cut face, which points toward you, so there are three drawers, one per storey.

After the parts were placed, I ran the two house rules: open faces are closed with solid end caps and the joints are locked with bolts. check_build reports no issues and the mesh-collision check reads "clear".

The build has 56 parts, more than the usual guide of about 40. The two three-storey columns, three drawers, caps and bolts account for it. The configurator's print estimate is about 3.0 kg of filament and about 4,450 minutes of printing.

When the half bases were placed, the configurator gave a LOOSE_BODY warning, which I didn't look into. The final check came back clean. When I looked at the build no props showed, as expected, since I added none.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
